summary: 奥克兰美术馆改建要同时修复老馆、扩建新馆，并改变年轻人觉得美术馆难以亲近的印象。文章沿建筑用材、毛利艺术、公园景观与参观人数评价改建成效。
logic: 从空间与访客检验成效

paragraphs.brief: 公共建筑项目的三重压力
sentences: Architects are finding it very difficult in today’s cultural landscape.
在当今的文化环境中，建筑师的工作处境颇为艰难。

The profession faces a three-way threat: a public that apparently doesn’t understand what architects do, developers who couldn’t care less what they do, and overbearing councils micromanaging every single aspect of what they do.
建筑师行业面临三方面的威胁：公众似乎不了解建筑师的工作，开发商对这些工作毫不在意，而强势的地方议会却对建筑师工作的每个细节横加干预。

According to sources within the architectural profession, the situation is much worse when architects work on municipal buildings, as architects FJMT and Archimedia discovered with their Auckland Gallery makeover, where a vast number of external pressures threatened the project, and with so many bureaucratic difficulties it looked doomed to fail.
业内人士认为，接手市政建筑时情况更糟，FJMT 和 Archimedia 两家事务所改建奥克兰美术馆时，就曾因外界压力和重重行政障碍而几乎无法推进项目。
paragraphs.gist: 公众不了解建筑师、开发商漠不关心、地方议会层层干预，这些压力在奥克兰美术馆这样的公共建筑改建中尤其突出。

paragraphs.brief: 修复老楼并吸引新观众
sentences: The major challenge of the gallery renovation project was that it involved two parts.
美术馆翻修项目的主要挑战是涉及两个部分。
The first was to restore the heritage building, dating back to 1888, which contained a network of small spaces, refurbished so often it contained 17 different floor heights.
首先要修复这座建于 1888 年的历史建筑，馆内遍布小空间，经过反复改造，地面竟有 17 种不同标高。
The second was to deliver a new extension that would not only double floor and exhibition space but also attract new patrons, a total necessity.
其次要建一座新翼，让建筑和展览面积翻倍，同时吸引新观众，这也是美术馆的迫切需要。
While the old building’s circulation was off-putting, so was something intangible yet just as powerful: its atmosphere.
老馆的参观路线让人望而却步，馆内的气氛虽说无形，也同样让人不想走进去。
For many, Auckland Art Gallery was just an old building that served a limited range of patrons with highbrow interests, missing its chance to engage with new audiences.
许多人眼中的奥克兰美术馆只是栋老楼，服务少数趣味高雅的常客，错失了与新观众接触的机会。
paragraphs.gist: 美术馆既要修复经过多次改造、地面高低错落的老楼，又要扩建展厅、吸引新观众，连原馆只服务少数人的印象也得改变。

paragraphs.brief: 年轻人为何不愿走进展馆
sentences: A 2003 survey of young people’s impressions of the gallery confirmed this opinion, sounding more like references to an abandoned building.
2003 年的调查证实了这一印象，年轻人对美术馆的描述听起来倒像在谈一栋废弃的建筑。

For the survey authors, ‘threshold fear’ – where certain groups are intimidated from entering certain spaces by their off-putting atmosphere – was the institution’s undoing, something no architect wants anything to do with.
调查者认为，这种令人却步的气氛使一些人不敢进门，这种“门槛恐惧”成了美术馆的致命弱点，也是建筑师唯恐造成的问题。
For those young people Auckland Art Gallery was undemocratic, ‘dusty’ and ‘cold’ – the epitome of threshold fear.
在这些年轻人眼中，奥克兰美术馆不够平易近人，显得“落满灰尘”又“冷冰冰的”，正是让人不敢进门的典型。
Also, 16 % of the sample group had no idea where it even was, despite being interviewed on the pavement right outside it.
还有 16% 的受访者连美术馆在哪里都不知道，尽管采访地点就在馆外的人行道上。

Clearly, the gallery was fatally out of step at a time when New Zealand’s national museum in Wellington was successfully engaging broader audiences with contemporary branding and marketing, interactive displays and temporary events.
同一时期，惠灵顿的新西兰国家博物馆已凭借现代化宣传、互动展览和短期活动吸引更多观众，奥克兰美术馆明显落在了后面。
paragraphs.gist: 受访青年觉得美术馆陈旧冷漠，甚至有人站在馆外仍不知道它在哪里，说明馆舍营造的距离感已挡住潜在观众。

paragraphs.brief: 八年筹建与贝壳杉争议
sentences: The decision to evolve the gallery was actually made in 2000, although it took eight years for building to commence, as the architects fought off heritage committees and conservationists trying to stop them.
改造计划早在 2000 年就已敲定，但遗产委员会和保护人士力图阻止，建筑师几经交涉，直到八年后才得以动工。
The architects were not just dealing with a disillusioned public, but also with precious timber and the parkland which surrounds the building.
建筑师既要面对失望的公众，也要顾及珍贵木材的使用以及建筑周围的公园绿地。
Pushing the design through the Environment Court, the body which approves renovations of this scale, alone took three years.
单是让负责审批这类大型改造的环境法院通过设计方案，就用了三年。
During this time the budget blew out by several million dollars, the funding dried up, and the new wing had to be completely redesigned.
在这段时间里，开支超出预算数百万，资金耗尽，新翼只得彻底重新设计。
Even after the redesign, the use of kauri timber, with its significance to New Zealand’s Māori* people, stirred up political debate.
即使在重新设计之后，使用对新西兰毛利人* 具有重要意义的Kauri木材也引发了政治辩论。
In the new building the architects have used kauri to produce a canopy with a curving interior roof supported by tapered, steel columns, also clad in kauri.
新馆用贝壳杉木建成带弧形内顶的顶棚，承托顶棚的锥形钢柱也包覆着这种木材。
The canopy represents a stag in full public face, its curvature filtering light to the forecourt to the west and creating a visual echo of the canopy of pohutukawa trees in Albert Park to the east.
顶棚像一头正面朝向公众的雄鹿，弧面把柔和的光线引向西侧前庭，在视觉上与东侧阿尔伯特公园的树冠呼应。
The park also has cultural significance to Māori as it was the site of early settlements.
该公园对毛利人也具有文化意义，因为它是早期定居点的所在地。
paragraphs.gist: 美术馆从决定改造到动工用了八年，保护争议、审批和资金不足迫使新翼重设，使用对毛利人意义重大的贝壳杉木也引发争论。

paragraphs.brief: 毛利艺术家和木材来源
sentences: The connection is reinforced by sculptures from Māori artist Arnold Wilson decorating the columns, while fellow artist Bernard Makoare was a consultant, ensuring the gallery emphasised Māori beliefs.
毛利艺术家阿诺德·威尔逊的雕塑装饰着柱子，加深了这一文化联系，另一位艺术家伯纳德·马科阿雷则担任顾问，使美术馆的设计体现毛利人的信仰。

Still that didn’t stop the conservationist Stephen King from accusing the architects of “throwing” kauri at a “mediocre building” and of misappropriating the ‘mana’ (spiritual energy) of the precious material (which is almost extinct: harvesting of both petrified and swamp kauri has been likened to a gold rush).
然而保护人士斯蒂芬·金仍批评建筑师把贝壳杉木“糟蹋”在一栋“平庸的建筑”上，挪用这种珍贵材料的灵力；这种木材现已十分稀少，采集石化木和沼泽古木的热潮堪比淘金。
However, the kauri that was used here was from the forest floor, and King’s misconceptions sum up the prejudice that surrounded the project.
不过，项目实际使用的是林地上的倒木，金的误解也反映出改建工程遭遇的偏见。
paragraphs.gist: 毛利艺术家通过柱上雕塑和设计咨询参与改造，仍有人批评用木浪费且不尊重传统，但建筑师实际选用的是林地上的倒木。

paragraphs.brief: 玻璃中庭连通展厅与公园
sentences: Objections also came from the Auckland Regional Council, worrying about the extension’s impact on Albert Park, yet the project’s relationship with parkland is one of the most successful outcomes.
奥克兰地区议会也曾反对扩建，担忧工程影响阿尔伯特公园，而美术馆与公园的结合后来成了改造最成功的地方之一。
Impact is not only minimal, but improves the park’s social function.
扩建对公园的扰动很小，还改善了它供人交往和活动的功能。

The extension’s enormous glass atrium opens up the building by directing the gaze from street level to the parkland beyond, while inside, the new art space is fronted along the east by a continuous glass wall incorporating the park into the gallery.
扩建部分的巨大玻璃中庭让人从街面就能望见后方的公园，新展厅东侧的连续玻璃墙又把公园景观引入馆中。

The glass becomes a ‘screen’ for viewing the outside world and makes the art accessible to those in the park, a far cry from both ‘white cube’ galleries worldwide – the plain boxes where paintings are hung in antiseptic white surroundings – and also the dusty, impermeable Auckland Gallery of old.
玻璃像一面展示外部景色的屏幕，也让公园中的人看得到艺术品，与只在素白封闭空间挂画的“白盒子”展馆以及旧馆沉闷封闭的模样形成鲜明对照。
paragraphs.gist: 地方议会曾担忧扩建破坏公园，建成后的玻璃中庭和通透外墙却让馆内外互相可见，也让公园里的行人能够接触艺术。

sentences: Another success is the refurbishment of the heritage building, especially the Mackelvie Gallery, in disrepair after its characteristic early-twentieth-century Edwardian decoration had been stripped out or walked away in previous renovations.
历史建筑的修复也是一大成果，尤其是麦凯维展厅，此前翻修时，其独具特色的 20 世纪初爱德华时代装饰或被拆掉，或已散失，展厅也日渐破败。

Remarkably, the Mackelvie space has been reconstructed from two old photos, although the problem of multiple floor levels was so serious that scaffolding had to be erected at the highest level, with work progressing downwards, the reverse of normal practice.
团队仅凭两张旧照便重建了麦凯维展厅，但各处地面高差甚大，只能打破惯例，把脚手架搭在最高处，再逐步向下施工。
When it was over, a fascinating detail was retained: the lowest level visible under glass embedded in the new floor.
当它结束时，保留了一个令人着迷的细节：在玻璃下可以看到的最低层嵌入新的地板。
The building itself is artwork, while elsewhere columns from the old gallery have been exposed in the walls of the new wing.
大楼本身是艺术品，而在其他地方，旧画廊的柱子被暴露在新楼的墙壁上。
paragraphs.gist: 修复团队依据两张旧照重建麦凯维展厅，从高处往下解决地面高差，还透过玻璃地板和裸露旧柱保留了建筑历次改造的痕迹。

paragraphs.brief: 重开后的访客人数变化
sentences: In 2008 the gallery averaged just 190,000 visitors annually.
2008年，画廊每年平均只有190,000人参观。
After reopening, it had 300,000 in five months.
重新开放后，美术馆仅五个月就接待了 30 万名访客。
Cynics will chalk that up to novelty of the new, but the fact is the gallery is now an alluring cultural space which is crawling with young people.
持怀疑态度的人会把参观人数激增归因于一时的新鲜感，但画廊如今确实成了颇有吸引力的文化空间，里面随处可见年轻人。
paragraphs.gist: 美术馆原先一年约接待十九万人，重开五个月就有三十万人到访，作者认为吸引力也来自改造后更具亲和力的空间。

items.en: What is the writer’s main point in the first paragraph?
items.zh: 第一段中，作者主要想说明什么？
correct: The most difficult projects for architects are public buildings.
对建筑师来说，公共建筑是最难做的项目。

items.en: The Auckland Gallery project was particularly difficult because
items.zh: 奥克兰画廊项目特别困难，因为
correct: it involved renovating the existing building and adding a new one.
项目既要翻修旧馆，又要为它增建新翼。

items.en: What disturbing information did the architects find out from the survey of young people?
items.zh: 建筑师从年轻人调查中发现了什么令人不安的信息？
correct: They did not visit the gallery because of the way it made them feel.
美术馆的氛围让他们望而却步。

items.en: What point is the writer making when he says that 16 % of the sample group did not know where the museum was?
items.zh: 作者特意指出 16% 的受访者不知道博物馆在哪里，是为了说明什么？
correct: The gallery was not reaching out to involve young people.
美术馆没有主动吸引年轻人参与。

items.en: Māori artists were used on this project to
items.zh: 项目请毛利艺术家参与，是为了什么？
correct: make sure the gallery respects Māori culture.
确保画廊尊重毛利人文化。

items.en: Before the renovation, the Auckland Art Gallery was regarded as an elitist institution.
items.zh: 在翻修之前，奥克兰美术馆被视为一个精英机构。
items.why: 改建前，许多人认为美术馆只服务于少数有高雅兴趣的顾客，未能吸引新观众，正是把它看作精英机构。

items.en: Stephen King’s intervention in the project shows his understanding of the architects’ use of kauri.
items.zh: 斯蒂芬·金介入这项工程，表明他了解建筑师如何使用贝壳杉木。
items.why: 作者说所用贝壳杉来自林地上已有的木材，明确把金对木材使用的理解称为“误解”。这与“他理解建筑师的做法”相反。

items.en: The way the building interacts with its surroundings is a triumph.
items.zh: 这座建筑与周围环境的结合是一项成功的设计。
items.why: 作者把新馆与邻近公园的关系称作项目最成功的方面之一，正面评价了建筑和环境之间的互动。

items.en: The glass screen along the east wall was one of the most costly items in the rebuild.
items.zh: 沿东墙的玻璃屏幕是重建中最昂贵的物品之一。
items.why: 文中描述玻璃幕墙如何让内外互相看见，讨论的是视觉效果。没有列出造价，也没有比较各项工程的费用。

items.en: The design of the extension to the Auckland Art Gallery is similar to the design of ‘white cube’ galleries in other parts of the world.
items.zh: 奥克兰美术馆的扩展设计与世界其他地区的 " 白色立方体 " 画廊的设计相似。
items.why: 玻璃中庭让参观者看见公园，也让园内的人看到艺术品。作者明确说这种开放的设计与封闭的“白盒子”展厅相去甚远。

groups.label: 观点判断 · YES / NO / NOT GIVEN

items.zh: 爱德华时代的装饰之所以遭到破坏，
items.answer: F · was the result of earlier attempts to modernise the building.
items.solution: 是早年试图使建筑现代化所造成的结果。

items.en: It is extraordinary that a limited number of photographs
items.zh: 令人惊叹的是，仅凭寥寥几张照片，
items.answer: C · was the clue to rebuilding the Mackelvie Gallery successfully.
items.solution: 便找到了成功复原麦凯维展厅的线索。

items.en: The problem of having so many floor levels to deal with
items.zh: 馆内各处地面标高不同，这一难题
items.answer: A · resulted in work being done in the opposite direction to that usually followed.
items.solution: 使施工团队不得不按与惯例相反的顺序作业。

items.en: The glass flooring in the Mackelvie Gallery which reveals old features
items.zh: 麦凯维展厅的玻璃地板显露出旧建筑的细节，这一设计
items.answer: D · has resulted in the building itself becoming a work of art.
items.solution: 导致大楼本身成为艺术品。

pairs: earlier attempts to modernise the building
原文用“先前的翻修”概括早期试图让建筑现代化的工程。
题干用形容词评价这件事，原文用副词引出同样令人惊讶的事实。
第 6 段 · 第 1 句
第 1 段 · 第 1 句
points: 文中描述玻璃幕墙如何让内外互相看见，讨论的是视觉效果。没有列出造价，也没有比较各项工程的费用。
题干问“爱德华时代的装饰之所以遭到破坏，”。定位句写到“历史建筑的修复也是一大成果，尤其是麦凯维展厅，此前翻修时，其独具特色的 20 世纪初爱德华时代装饰或被拆掉，或已散失，展厅也日渐破败”。
clauses: …, so was something intangible yet just as powerful: its atmosphere.
连接词 while 引出“While the old building’s circulation was off-putting”，说明主句的时间或对比关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 while 把这一层关系补进去。
For many, Auckland Art Gallery was just an old building …, missing its chance to engage with new audiences.
“that served a limited range of patrons with highbrow interests”修饰前面的 building。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 that 时，回看 building，再把修饰信息接回主句。
lead: The renovated Auckland Art Gallery in New Zealand unites old and new, creating an irresistible urge to step inside
改造后的新西兰奥克兰美术馆融汇新旧，让人忍不住想走进去。
vocabulary: 主张保护历史建筑的人
